newsitem.title: FRANCE: Iranian exiles protest in Paris against Tehran.
newsitem.headline: Iranian exiles protest in Paris against Tehran.

text.p: Several hundred opponents of Iran's government demonstrated in a Paris cemetery on Friday to protest against Tehran's alleged harassing of exiles, police said.

The protest in the Pere Lachaise cemetery marked the first anniversary of the assassination of Zahra Rajabi, a Paris-based leader of the National Coucil of Resistance of Iran. She was gunned down in Istanbul, Turkey, on Februray 20, 1996.
Demonstrators denounced the "marked increase in Iranian-sponsored terrorism and Europe's lenient policy towards it", a National Council of Resistance statement said.

Iranian dissidents accuse Tehran of sending commandos to Europe to kill their leaders. French intelligence sources recently reported that Iran's secret services were increasingly active in cracking down on opponents.

"For more than a year now, the threats have chiefly targeted exiles in Germany," a police source told Reuters. "In France, the threat does exist, but it was toned down when a leading spokeswoman for the National council, Myriam Radjavi, left some months ago to join her husband in Iraq".

Eight Iranian exiles have been killed in France and several dozen in other countries since the 1979 revolution. Opponents of the Tehran government say it was behind the murders. Iran denies involvement.
